source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A self-protective way of explaining the job loss that lets the client save face, rather than an accurate read of how the client actually felt about the job","B":"Reaction formation, expressing the opposite of a true feeling, which does not describe this particular self-serving explanation being offered","C":"Projection, attributing one's own feelings to another, which does not describe this particular pattern of self-justification","D":"Sublimation, redirecting an urge into an acceptable outlet, which does not describe this particular verbal explanation being offered"}}
source_row.rationale: Rationalization is a defense mechanism in which a person creates logical-sounding, but ultimately self-serving, explanations to justify a behavior, feeling, or outcome, avoiding acknowledgment of a true, more uncomfortable underlying reason (such as job loss due to their own tardiness) — a common, often unconscious way of protecting self-esteem.
source_row.source_detail: Recognition of Rationalization as a Defense Mechanism
source_row.stem: A client who was terminated from their job for repeated tardiness explains, "I didn't really want that job anyway; it wasn't a good fit for me," and a family member takes this explanation at face value as the client's genuine, accurate assessment.
